name: STM32WL55CCU6
title: Dual-core Arm Cortex-M4/M0+ microcontroller with sub-GHz LoRa, (G)FSK, (G)MSK and BPSK radio, 256 KB flash, 64 KB SRAM
summary: The STM32WL55 and STM32WL54 put a 150 to 960 MHz sub-GHz transceiver beside a 48 MHz Cortex-M4 (CPU1) and a 48 MHz Cortex-M0+ (CPU2), with 256 KB of flash and 64 KB of SRAM. The radio sends and receives LoRa (STM32WL55 only) and (G)FSK, and sends (G)MSK and BPSK, through a +15 dBm low-power PA and a +22 dBm high-power PA. An on-chip SMPS or LDO makes the 1.55 V core and radio supply from a 1.8 V to 3.6 V input; the parts add a 12-bit ADC, a 12-bit DAC, two comparators, AES-256, PKA, RNG and secure services on CPU2. They come in a 7 x 7 mm UFQFPN48 and a 5 x 5 mm UFBGA73.
key_figures: Cortex-M4 with DSP and MPU, 48 MHz, 1.25 DMIPS/MHz; Cortex-M0+ with MPU, 48 MHz, 0.95 DMIPS/MHz
256 KB flash with ECC, 32 KB SRAM1 + 32 KB SRAM2
-123 dBm 2-FSK at 1.2 Kbit/s; -148 dBm LoRa at 10.4 kHz, SF12
4.82 mA typ, LoRa 125 kHz, SMPS on
Shutdown 31 nA, Standby 360 nA, Stop 2 with RTC 1 µA typ at 3 V
-40 to 85 °C ambient (suffix 6) or -40 to 105 °C (suffix 7, radio to 85 °C)

circuits.title: Power supply scheme
circuits.description: VDD, VDDRF and VDDSMPS share one supply. Each VDD pin has 100 nF and the rail one 4.7 µF; VDDSMPS has its own 4.7 µF. The SMPS switches VLXSMPS into a 15 µH inductor and a 470 nF capacitor to make the 1.55 V VFBSMPS rail, which also feeds VDDRF1V55. VDDA takes 10 nF plus 1 µF, VREF+ 100 nF plus 1 µF, and VBAT a 1.55 V to 3.6 V backup source. VDDPA is on VDDSMPS, the connection for the high-power PA. Every capacitor sits at or under its pin pair.
notes: VDD, VSS and VSSRF each have several pins, and each net takes all of them.
VDDPA goes to VDDSMPS for the high-power PA, or to VDDRF1V55 (VFBSMPS) for the low-power PA.
In the UFQFPN48, VREF+ is joined to VDDA inside and the exposed pad is VSS.
Without the SMPS, the inductor between VLXSMPS and VFBSMPS can be left off.

operation.text: STM32WL55 parts carry the LoRa modem; STM32WL54 parts have every other modulation but not LoRa. C parts come in the UFQFPN48 with 29 GPIOs and 9 external ADC channels; J parts in the UFBGA73 with 43 GPIOs, 12 external ADC channels and a VREF+ pin with VREFBUF. All have 256 KB flash and 64 KB SRAM.

CPU1 is a Cortex-M4 with DSP instructions and CPU2 a Cortex-M0+, each with its own MPU and both up to 48 MHz. The radio talks to the cores over an internal SPI (SUBGHZSPI). The RF low-layer stack runs on either core, the host application preferably on CPU1, and all secure code on CPU2. A hardware semaphore block (HSEM, 16 semaphores) and an inter-processor communication controller (IPCC, six channels each way) link the two cores; the IPCC data itself lives in shared memory.
An instruction prefetch queue and branch cache in front of the 64-bit flash give CPU1 the equivalent of zero-wait-state execution up to 48 MHz on CoreMark, close to 60 DMIPS.
Each core's MPU manages up to eight regions, each split into eight subregions, from 32 bytes up to the full 4 GB address space. It is optional and can be bypassed.

One bank of up to 256 KB in 2 KB pages, read and written 72 bits at a time (64 data plus 8 ECC bits), with page and mass erase. ECC corrects single errors, detects double errors and logs the failing address in FLASH_ECCR. The flash is shared by the two CPUs in time; either CPU can suspend a write or erase. A part of the flash can be reserved for CPU2, out of CPU1's reach.

Readout protection has three levels: 0 none; 1 blocks flash access while debug is connected or the part boots from SRAM or the bootloader; 2 disables debug, SRAM boot and bootloader selection for good, and only the secure CPU2 can undo it. Write protection covers two areas at 4 KB granularity. PCROP makes two areas execute-only at 2 KB granularity, and the PCROP_RDP bit picks whether they are erased when RDP drops from level 1 to 0.

SRAM1 (32 KB) sits at 0x2000 0000 and SRAM2 (32 KB) at 0x2000 8000, contiguous with SRAM1 and mirrored at 0x1000 0000. SRAM2 has hardware parity and can be kept in Standby. Both are read and written with no wait states at any CPU clock.

Security blocks include a securable RNG, customer key storage, flash and SRAM partitions reachable only by CPU2, a securable radio subsystem, securable DMA channels, AES with 128 and 256-bit keys (ECB, CBC, CTR, GCM, GMAC, CCM), and a PKA for modular exponentiation up to 3136 bits and ECC scalar multiplication and ECDSA up to 521 bits. The GTZC sets the secure and privileged state of peripherals and memory areas and routes illegal-access events to a secure interrupt on CPU2. CPU2 runs the secure services: a unique boot entry, the sub-GHz MAC layer in secure form, firmware update and install (SFU, SFI), and key management. Each part has a 64-bit UID (IEEE 802-2001) and a 96-bit die ID.

The BOOT0 pin and the BOOT1 option bit choose between user flash, the system memory bootloader, SRAM, and the system memory holding the SFI. The bootloader loads code over USART or SPI. If BOOT0 asks for flash but the first flash word is empty, the part boots the bootloader instead, which reconfigures some GPIOs (AN2606); setting nSWBOOT0 = 0 and nBOOT0 = 1 forces boot from flash and turns this off.

The transceiver covers 150 to 960 MHz continuously. LoRa runs from 7.8 to 500 kHz bandwidth, spreading factor 5 to 12, 0.013 to 17.4 Kbit/s; FSK and GFSK from 0.6 to 300 Kbit/s; (G)MSK transmit from 0.1 to 10 Kbit/s; BPSK transmit at 100 and 600 bit/s. It is controlled by commands over SUBGHZSPI, reports events by interrupts, and signals BUSY while it cannot take a command. It meets LoRaWAN v1.0 and ETSI EN 300 220, EN 300 113, EN 301 166, FCC CFR 47 parts 15, 24, 90 and 101, and ARIB STD-T30, T-67 and T-108.

The modem modulates the RF-PLL directly, with optional pre-filtering, and the PLL drives one of two PAs. The high-power PA on RFO_HP gives up to +22 dBm; its regulator must then be fed from VDD on VDDPA, and the maximum power falls with that supply: +22 dBm at 3.3 V, +20 dBm at 2.7 V, +19 dBm at 2.4 V, +16 dBm at 1.8 V. The low-power PA on RFO_LP gives up to +15 dBm across the whole 1.8 V to 3.6 V range, its regulator fed from the 1.55 V VFBSMPS rail. Output power steps in 32 steps of about 1 dB, and the PA ramp time is programmable.

A differential LNA feeds a quadrature mixer down to a low IF, then low-pass filters and a sigma-delta ADC; decimation, further down-conversion, channel filtering and demodulation are digital. The wanted signal sits at the LO plus the IF. I/Q calibration, run at start-up and on command, improves image rejection. The receiver works at low IF except for some wide bandwidths (LORA_BW_500 at zero IF).

The RF-PLL, self-calibrating, makes the LO for both directions from the 32 MHz HSE32 reference. HSE32 takes a 32 MHz crystal (NX2016SA or NX1612SA) with internal trimming capacitors, or a clipped-sine TCXO powered from PB0-VDD_TCXO through the internal 1.6 V to 3.3 V regulator and coupled into OSC_IN through 220 Ω and a series capacitor.

Integrated passive devices from the BALF-WL range combine matching, filtering and balun for each package and main use: 22 dBm at 915 MHz, 15 dBm at 868/915 MHz and 17 dBm at 490 MHz, on 2 or 4-layer boards. Reference designs are in data brief DB4597.

VDD (1.8 V to 3.6 V) feeds the I/Os and system analog blocks. VDDSMPS and VDDRF (1.8 V to 3.6 V) are fed from the VDD supply itself. The 1.55 V typical VFBSMPS rail (1.45 V to 1.62 V) is the output of the SMPS step-down and feeds the main regulator; VDDRF1V55 is wired to it. VDDA (0 V to 3.6 V) feeds the ADC, DAC, VREFBUF and comparators, independent of VDD and best tied to VDD when they are unused. VBAT (1.55 V to 3.6 V) keeps the RTC, TAMP, LSE and backup registers alive when VDD is absent. An internal regulator makes VCORE for the logic and SRAMs.

While VDD is below 1 V, VDDA must stay within 300 mV above VDD; during power-down VDD may briefly fall below the other supplies if the energy delivered stays under 1 mJ. Above 1 V the other supplies are independent of VDD. VDD falls no faster than 10 µs/V.

An LDO and an SMPS step-down work in parallel to make VFBSMPS; switching the SMPS on only changes efficiency. The MCU picks the mode with SMPSEN in PWR_CR5, and the radio with its SetRegulatorMode() command; SMPS has priority, and LDO mode is selected after every POR and NRST reset. While the radio is active the mode does not change until the radio activity ends. In Stop 1, Stop 2 and Standby with the radio idle, both are off. SMPSRDY in PWR_SR2 shows the mode. The radio registers set the SMPS maximum load current (SUBGHZ_SMPSC2R) and the LDO and SMPS inrush (SUBGHZ_PCR).

The SMPS needs its clock: if the clock stops, the device can be destroyed. Clock detection, which switches the SMPS off and the LDO on when the clock fails, is off by default and must be enabled with SUBGHZ_SMPSC0R.CLKDE before the SMPS is turned on.

POR/PDR and BOR0 cannot be disabled; BOR works in every mode but Shutdown. Five BOR thresholds, from about 1.7 V (BOR0) to 2.9 V (BOR4), are chosen by option bytes; BOR holds the part in reset until VDD passes the threshold and resets it when VDD drops below. The PVD compares VDD with seven thresholds (1.9 to 2.9 V) and interrupts on either crossing; set to its lowest level with EWPVD in PWR_CR3 it can watch the VDD needed by the radio and wake the part on a drop. PVM3 watches VDDA against 1.65 V. A radio end-of-life monitor flags VDD too low for the radio (about 1.9 V), at which point software must stop radio activity.

The main regulator runs in range 1 (system clock up to 48 MHz, fastest flash read) or range 2 (up to 16 MHz, slower flash read); flash write and erase work in both. The low-power regulator takes over in the low-power modes. After reset the part is in Run, range 1.

VBAT takes over automatically when VDD is gone and powers the RTC, LSE and backup registers from a battery, a supercapacitor or VDD. Three tamper pins stay active. An internal charger, through 5 kΩ or 1.5 kΩ (VBRS), can charge VBAT while VDD is present. On VBAT alone, external interrupts and RTC events do not end VBAT operation.

Sleep stops the CPU clock only. LPRun runs below 2 MHz on the low-power regulator, and LPSleep is entered from it. Stop 0 and Stop 1 keep SRAM and all registers with the VCORE clocks stopped and PLL, MSI, HSI16 and HSE32 off; LSI and LSE may run, the RTC may stay on, and Stop 0 keeps the main regulator for the fastest wakeup at much higher current. Stop 2 powers off part of VCORE, keeping SRAM1, SRAM2, the CPUs and some peripherals. These Stop modes wake on MSI up to 48 MHz or HSI16. Standby powers VCORE off, optionally keeping SRAM2 on the low-power regulator (RRS in PWR_CR3); Shutdown also turns LSI off and disables supply monitoring. Both wake on MSI at 4 MHz. The radio can stay active in every mode except Shutdown, where it is held in Deep-sleep.

During and after reset the I/Os are analog (Schmitt trigger off), except the five JTAG/SWD pins, which come up with pull-up or pull-down. The internal pull-up on NRST is turned off when the reset source is internal. NRST must be able to go below VIL(NRST) max for a reset to register.

SYSCLK comes from HSI16 (16 MHz RC, ±1 % trimmed), MSI (100 kHz to 48 MHz RC, 12 ranges, can lock to LSE), HSE32 (32 MHz crystal or TCXO) or the PLL. After reset the system runs on MSI at 4 MHz. LSI (32 kHz RC) and LSE (32.768 kHz crystal) serve the RTC, the IWDG (always LSI) and low-power peripherals. The AHB and APB clocks are 48 MHz at most. U(S)ARTs wake the part from Stop only on HSI16 or LSE, I2Cs only on HSI16, LPTIMs and the RTC only on LSI or LSE (or an external clock for LPTIM). Clock security systems watch HSE32 and LSE.

LSE has four drive levels (LSEDRV), from 250 nA to 630 nA; the crystal's critical gm must be below the level's Gmcritmax. Fit the crystal and load capacitors close to the pins, and never fit a resistor between OSC32_IN and OSC32_OUT. In bypass mode the LSE oscillator is off and OSC32_IN takes an external clock of 21.2 to 44.4 kHz.

Each GPIO can be a push-pull or open-drain output, an input (floating, pulled up or pulled down), or an alternate function, and its configuration can be locked. GPIOs sit on AHB2 for fast toggling. They sink or source up to ±8 mA, or ±20 mA with relaxed VOL and VOH, within the device's total current ratings. PC13 to PC15 run from the backup power switch, which sinks only 3 mA. Unused or floating inputs are best set to analog or tied to a level, to avoid extra current.

Two DMA controllers with seven channels each (14 in all) reach any DMA-capable peripheral through DMAMUX1, with four software priority levels, up to 65536 data per transfer, and secure or privileged channels. CPU1's NVIC has 16 priority levels and up to 62 maskable channels; CPU2's has 4 levels and up to 32. The EXTI turns peripheral and pin events into wakeups, interrupts and events for either CPU.

One 12-bit SAR ADC, 2.5 Msps, up to 16 bits with hardware oversampling of up to 256 samples, with up to 12 external channels and four internal (temperature sensor on VIN[12], VREFINT on VIN[13], VBAT/3 on VIN[14], DAC output). It converts single or in scan mode, shuts itself down between conversions, has an analog watchdog, can be triggered by timers and served by DMA, and runs over the whole VDD range. When VDDA is below 2.4 V the I/O analog switch booster must be on (BOOSTEN).

The sensor's output is linear in temperature; each part is calibrated at 30 °C and 130 °C (TS_CAL1, TS_CAL2), and without calibration it suits only relative readings. VREFINT, about 1.212 V, is measured per part at 30 °C and stored as VREFINT_CAL. Both values are taken with VDDA = VREF+ = 3.3 V.

The DAC has one 12-bit buffered channel, 8 or 12-bit modes, noise and triangle generation, DMA and timer or external triggers, and a low-power sample-and-hold mode with an internal or external capacitor, clocked from LSI. VREFBUF gives 2.048 V (VDDA ≥ 2.4 V) or 2.5 V (VDDA ≥ 2.8 V) on VREF+ for the ADC, DAC and outside parts, with 0.5 to 1.5 µF of load including 100 nF; with it off, an external reference can drive VREF+. Two rail-to-rail comparators take an I/O or VREFINT and its 1/4, 1/2, 3/4 steps as reference, with programmable hysteresis and speed, can form a window comparator and wake the part from Stop.

TIM1 is a 16-bit advanced timer with four channels, three complementary outputs with dead time and break inputs. TIM2 is a 32-bit four-channel timer with encoder support; TIM16 and TIM17 are 16-bit with one channel and one complementary output. LPTIM1 (Stop 0 to Stop 2) and LPTIM2, LPTIM3 (Stop 0 and Stop 1) run from LSE, LSI or an external clock and can wake the part; LPTIM1 has an encoder mode. The IWDG (12-bit, LSI clocked) keeps running in Stop and Standby; the WWDG (7-bit) runs from the main clock with an early warning interrupt. Each core has a 24-bit SysTick.

The BCD calendar RTC with alarms and a 32-bit sub-second wakeup counter runs through every mode, reset and VBAT while the supply is in range. Twenty 32-bit backup registers survive all low-power modes and VBAT and are protected by tamper detection; there are three tamper pins and four internal tampers.

Three I2Cs (Sm, Fm, Fm+ at 1 Mbit/s with 20 mA drive, SMBus 2.0, PMBus 1.1) wake the part on address match; I2C3 also from Stop 2. Two USARTs reach 4 Mbit/s with LIN, IrDA, smartcard (ISO 7816), SPI master mode, RS485 driver enable and wakeup from Stop at up to 200 kbaud. LPUART1 wakes from Stop at up to 220 kbaud and runs at 9600 baud from LSE alone. Two SPIs run to 16 Mbit/s, SPI2S2 also as I2S (Philips, MSB, LSB, PCM). SUBGHZSPI only controls the radio.

The SWJ-DP serves both serial-wire (two pins, SWDIO on PA13 and SWCLK on PA14) and five-pin JTAG; a TMS sequence switches between them, and freed JTAG pins become GPIOs. The two CPUs have cross-trigger support.

Voltages are referred to VSS. Characterization is done on the UFQFPN48. Minimum and maximum values hold over temperature, supply and frequency, tested on every part at 25 °C and TAmax unless a note says they come from characterization (mean ±3σ). Typical values are at 25 °C with VDD = VDDA = VBAT = 3 V and are not tested; typical ADC accuracy is mean ±2σ. Pins are loaded with 50 pF for pin measurements.

PD maximum is 392 mW (UFBGA73) at 85 °C for suffix 6 or 105 °C for suffix 7; at lower TA more power is allowed while TJ stays within its maximum. Junction limits are 105 °C (suffix 6) and 125 °C (suffix 7). θJA is 43.4 °C/W for the UFBGA73 and 27.4 °C/W for the UFQFPN48.

Each supply pair is decoupled with ceramic capacitors as close as possible to, or under, its pins. The UFQFPN48 exposed pad is VSS and must be soldered to the ground plane. The NRST capacitor sits as close to the device as possible. A large parasitic capacitance on an ADC input degrades accuracy unless fADC is lowered.
